59: Such is the proper reading: It is needed [to teach] that he can perform levirate marriage without her consent - which is how we expound [the verse] in Tractate Yevamot [Yevamot 8b:14].

If so - if [the verse] is to teach that sexual intercourse [is the only method of acquisition], let it say "and perform levirate marriage." What [then is connoted by] "and perform levirate marriage with her"? To derive that it can also [be done] against her will. This is taught explicitly in a baraita in Tractate Yevamot in Chapter "One who had Intercourse with his Yevama": "And perform levirate marriage" -- sexual intercourse completes her [acquisition], but money and a marriage document do not complete her [acquisition]. "And consummate the levirate marriage with her” -- [he acquires her even if he acted] against her will [Yevamot 54a:5].
